threads.body:
I'm a bit skeptical of this approach with `suspend()`, it feels like a bit of a hack because of all the getattr calls and I noticed we set the span in context in `__init__()` for the invocations. Are we solving this problem where python generators leak their context accidentally, or is it related to the `__init__()` thing? For reference, [logfire docs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/logfire/reference/generators/#_top) describe the problem well.

AI suggestions below on how to fix it, but LMK if I'm missing something:

---

1. `SyncStreamWrapper.__init__` isn't always called in the same context frame that created `invocation`. For deferred parsing like `with_raw_response` in `anthropic/_raw_response.py`, `MessagesStreamWrapper` is only constructed later when the caller calls `raw.parse()`. If `raw.parse()` runs under a child span or in another task, calling `invocation.suspend()` inside `super().__init__` detaches the outer invocation token out of order and leaves `invocation.span` stuck as the current span when the child span exits (the same bug #817 had to work around in `openai/_raw_response.py`).
2. All the `getattr(invocation, ...)` / `hasattr(invocation, ...)` duck-typing in `stream.py` (`suspend`, `_suspended`, `_request_stream`) feels like a sign that the protocol boundary between `GenAIInvocation` and `SyncStreamWrapper` isn't right. `super().__init__(stream, invocation)` also still conflates LLM chunk-timing metrics (`_on_stream_chunk`) with context scoping, so agent stream wrappers (`smolagents`, `qwen-agent`, `agno`) still can't pass `invocation` to `super().__init__`.
3. Taking a step back, `suspend()` only has to exist because `GenAIInvocation.__init__` eagerly calls `attach()` on construction instead of only attaching in `__enter__` (for `with invocation:` callers) or `activate()` (for stream `_advance()` steps).

Could we revert the `util-genai` change here to keep this PR scoped to `google-genai`, and open a separate issue to clean up the `GenAIInvocation` / `SyncStreamWrapper` context lifecycle and protocol properly?

replies.body:
That makes sense. I originally moved it into the base wrapper to avoid duplication, but the deferred `parse()` case means the constructor isn’t always a safe place to detach the original context.

The issues are connected. Invocation construction makes the span current, and returning or yielding from a stream doesn’t restore the caller’s context.

I’ll revert the shared util change and keep the suspension in the Google GenAI implementation for this PR, along with the regression tests. I’ll open a follow-up issue for separating span creation from activation, and context handling from chunk timing metrics.
